Hi Tina —

Thanks again for the quick demo earlier. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can align with your security/compliance team before the pilot:

Recap (from our call)
- Use case: Clearline will send clinical notes and anonymized patient attributes to Redwood to power classification and short summaries during triage.
- Volume: ~200k API calls/month initially, spiky daytime traffic.
- Requirement highlights: no persistent storage of raw patient PII; audit logs accessible to Clearline; control plane in US-only region; DSAR / deletion within 30 days of request.

Clarifying questions (need explicit answers for your security team)
1) Prompt inputs: do you need confirmation of whether prompt inputs are written to disk, and if so where (S3 buckets region)?
2) Prompt outputs / generated text: do you consider generated summaries to be PII-containing outputs that must be deleted on request, or will Clearline classify which outputs are sensitive?
3) Logging: do you need full request/response logging with request IDs and partial user identifiers, or just aggregated telemetry?
4) Retention windows: you mentioned "short-term retention for debugging" — can you confirm max allowed retention (days) for request payloads and generated outputs?

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll gather explicit, bulletized answers from our infra/security and send a single-sheet summary you can share with your SecOps.
- If needed, we can offer an opt-in configuration for zero-retention mode in the pilot (no request/response persistence) or a dedicated private deployment.
- Send over the security checklist (if you haven't already) and we’ll map fields to our controls.

If you can reply inline to the questions above that will speed things up. I’m looping Sam (legal) for visibility.

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our end (inline):

> 1) Prompt inputs: do you need confirmation of whether prompt inputs are written to disk, and if so where (S3 buckets region)?
Yes — our SecOps wants to know exactly what is persisted by default (raw prompt, metadata, user/email identifiers) and the physical residency (AWS region / account). We also want to understand if data ever crosses regions for routing/failover.

> 2) Prompt outputs / generated text: do you consider generated summaries to be PII-containing outputs that must be deleted on request, or will Clearline classify which outputs are sensitive?
Generated summaries may contain PHI. For compliance we need the ability to: (a) request deletion of outputs tied to a user or record ID; (b) receive a deletion audit that shows the action and timestamp.

> 3) Logging: do you need full request/response logging with request IDs and partial user identifiers, or just aggregated telemetry?
We need request-level logs for investigations (request ID, timestamp, routing decision, model variant). The logs should NOT include raw patient identifiers unless they are encrypted & access-controlled.

> 4) Retention windows: you mentioned "short-term retention for debugging" — can you confirm max allowed retention (days) for request payloads and generated outputs?
SecOps suggested: max 30 days for raw payloads, max 90 days for request/response metadata/logs. If you have an option for shorter retention or a no-retention pilot, please flag that.

Attaching our security checklist (redacted).

Thanks,
Tina Morales
Head of Data Privacy | Clearline Analytics
Attachments: clearline-security-checklist.xlsx

Jordan / Lauren —

Draft language below that we can send to Clearline. I also attached a short retention matrix that maps object types to default and optional retention windows.

Engineer/security summary (bulletized):
- Prompt inputs (raw request payloads): stored encrypted at rest in US (us-east-1) S3 by default; default retention = 30 days; optional: zero-retention flag (pilot) or private deployment where Redwood does not persist payloads.
- Prompt outputs (generated text): stored only if customer enables output persistence; default hosted behavior: outputs are persisted for 30 days to allow debugging and quality monitoring; we will mark outputs that include PHI and provide deletion-on-request.
- Logs/telemetry: request-level logs (request_id, model_variant, timestamp, routing decision) kept for 90 days; logs do NOT include raw patient identifiers unless the customer sends them in the payload (we can offer client-side tokenization).
- Deletion/DSARs: we provide an API for targeted deletion (by request_id or customer_record_id) and a deletion audit that returns timestamp + initiating actor. Deletions are propagated to indices and caches; full wipe (for private deployment) is available as part of the onboarding playbook.
- Cross-region behavior: control plane remains in US; failover may route inference to other US zones but not EU/APAC unless explicitly configured.

Suggested legal phrasing (for DPA addendum):
- "Redwood will persist request payloads and generated outputs only for the retention periods agreed to in this Addendum. Redwood will provide an API to request deletion of data associated with specified customer record identifiers. Redwood will supply a deletion audit report upon completion of a deletion request."

Attachments: redwood-data-retention-matrix.csv

If that looks good I can tidy into a single-page PDF and we can send to Tina with the attachments.
